concerns.text: FR-004 states that a 'successful fix' MUST be validated by an exact ground‑truth vector match, yet Acceptance Scenario 4 (User Story 2) claims the system can flag a task as 'success' based solely on the semantic similarity score (≥ 0.95) even when the vector match fails. This logical contradiction makes the definition of the primary outcome ambiguous and invalidates any downstream analysis.

FR-005 adds a semantic equivalence check (score ≥ 0.95) as a secondary success metric, but because FR-004 already requires an exact vector match, any case that satisfies FR-004 will automatically satisfy the semantic check (semantic similarity = 1). Thus the semantic check is redundant and creates a tautological validation component, turning part of the success criterion into a trivial function of the predictor.

The study treats 'cognitive load' as being fully captured by the proxies 'time‑to‑success' and 'iteration count'. Established HCI practice typically augments these objective measures with subjective (e.g., NASA‑TLX) or physiological data to ensure construct validity. Relying solely on latency/iterations threatens the validity of the claimed cognitive‑load findings.
